name: Ross 248
sources: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/ (SIMBAD TAP basic table: RA/Dec J2000, parallax)
notes: Distance from Gaia DR3 parallax 316.48 mas (SIMBAD). Mass and age (2.6 Gyr) from Mann et al. 2015 via Wikipedia; spectral type M6V cited on Wikipedia (SIMBAD lists M5.0V). candidates.name: eps Eri c
candidates.note: Proposed from clumps in the outer debris disk at ~40-50 AU; brightest clumps later identified as background sources, existence debated. Not in NASA archive.

sources: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/ (SIMBAD TAP basic table: RA/Dec J2000, parallax)
notes: Planet b values are the NASA archive default solution (Thompson et al. 2025, AJ 170, 301): a=3.53 AU, P=2680 d, true mass 1.0 Jupiter mass (=317.8 Earth masses, not minimum, from combined RV+astrometry). Other solutions in archive give ~0.6-0.7 MJ. Detection was long controversial but is now considered confirmed. Age: most estimates 200-800 Myr per Wikipedia; one more recent estimate is 1.1+/-0.1 Gyr; NASA archive lists 0.6 Gyr. Has a well-known debris disk (rings at ~3 AU and ~64 AU). Planet radii set to null: none of these planets transit; the radii in the NASA archive pscomppars table are 'Calculated Value' estimates from a mass-radius relation, not measurements.

sources: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/ (SIMBAD TAP basic table: RA/Dec J2000, parallax)
notes: Archive host name is 'GJ 887'. b and c discovered by Jeffers et al. 2020 (Science); d (50.8 d, habitable-zone) was a candidate in 2020 and confirmed with e by Hartogh et al. 2026 (A&A 707, A93), which is the archive default for all four. Mass 0.479 Msun (Pineda 2021, Wikipedia); archive lists 0.495. Age poorly constrained: Wikipedia cites 4.57 Gyr, NASA archive lists 2.9 Gyr. Spectral type M0.5V (Wikipedia) vs M1V (archive) vs M2V (SIMBAD). Planet radii set to null: none of these planets transit; the radii in the NASA archive pscomppars table are 'Calculated Value' estimates from a mass-radius relation, not measurements.

name: Ross 128
sources: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/ (SIMBAD TAP basic table: RA/Dec J2000, parallax)
notes: Planet b discovered 2017 (Bonfils et al. 2018, archive default). Wikipedia mentions a ~1.8 Earth-mass / ~1.6 Earth-radius estimate, but that is model-based; only m sin i = 1.4 is measured. Age ~5 Gyr is approximate (Wikipedia and archive both give ~5). Mass 0.176 Msun per Wikipedia; archive lists 0.168. Planet radii set to null: none of these planets transit; the radii in the NASA archive pscomppars table are 'Calculated Value' estimates from a mass-radius relation, not measurements.

name: EZ Aquarii

components.name: EZ Aquarii C (Gl 866 C, also called Ab)

sources: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/ (SIMBAD TAP basic table: RA/Dec J2000, parallax)
notes: Distance from parallax 293.6+/-0.9 mas (Torres 2010 compilation via SIMBAD); no Gaia parallax used, so distance uncertainty ~0.03 ly. Structure: A and C form a 3.79-day spectroscopic binary (~0.03 AU); B orbits the AC pair every ~823 days (~1.2 AU, e~0.44). Masses from Torres et al. 2010 (alternate Popova & Shevchenko 2016: Aa 0.1216, Ab 0.0957). Total ~0.326 Msun. Only A has a published spectral subtype (M5V); B and C are just 'M' dwarfs per RECONS. No age found. No planets or planet claims; Wikipedia notes a circumbinary habitable-zone orbit is dynamically possible.

sources: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/ (SIMBAD TAP basic table: RA/Dec J2000, parallax)
notes: Distance from Gaia DR3 parallax ~286.0 mas. Masses from NEID 2025 (via Wikipedia). Age not well constrained: Kervella et al. 2008 evolutionary models give 6.0-6.1+/-1.0 Gyr (the commonly quoted value), gyrochronology ~2.0 Gyr, chromospheric activity 2.4-3.8 Gyr, kinematics ~10 Gyr. Use '6' if a single number is required, with caveats.

name: Procyon
sources: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/ (SIMBAD TAP basic table: RA/Dec J2000, parallax)
notes: Distance from Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax 284.56+/-1.26 mas, so +/-0.05 ly uncertainty. Masses and system age 1.87+/-0.13 Gyr from Bond et al. 2015 (HST astrometry). Procyon B white-dwarf cooling age ~1.37 Gyr (Giammichele 2012). A and B orbit every ~40.8 yr. No planets or planet claims.

name: Groombridge 34
sources: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/ (SIMBAD TAP basic table: RA/Dec J2000, parallax)
notes: Both planets listed as confirmed in NASA archive (default: Pinamonti et al. 2018). Planet b was announced by Howard et al. 2014 at m sin i ~5.35 Earth masses, then questioned when CARMENES did not detect it; Pinamonti 2018 recovered it at a lower m sin i (3.03). Planet c is poorly constrained (m sin i 36 +25/-18 Earth masses, P ~7600 d / ~21 yr). Age ~3 Gyr is a rough estimate (Wikipedia, ref ApJ 804, 64); archive gives none. Mass A 0.393 (Pineda 2021), B 0.15 (Pinamonti 2018).

name: DX Cancri
sources: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/ (SIMBAD TAP basic table: RA/Dec J2000, parallax)
notes: Distance from Gaia DR3 parallax 279.25 mas. Mass 0.106+/-0.009 Msun (CARMENES, via Wikipedia). Age 200 Myr assumes membership in the Castor Moving Group, which is itself questioned as a real coeval group, so treat it as uncertain. Not in NASA archive; no planet claims found.
